name: Biblical Word Study
description: Investigate a biblical word in its original language and contexts without assuming one meaning in every occurrence.

sections.title: Word and question
sections.guidance: Identify the Hebrew or Greek lemma, spelling and the particular passage or question. A translated English word may represent several different original words.
formerGuidance: The word being studied, its original form and how translations render it.
The word or expression being studied, and how translations render it.

sections.title: Occurrences and translations
sections.guidance: Find representative occurrences of this lemma and note how translators render it. Distinguish the lemma from inflected forms and other words with similar translations.
formerGuidance: Where the word appears. (Automatic occurrence lists arrive with the concordance.)
Where the word appears; the concordance can list its occurrences.

sections.title: Range of meanings
sections.guidance: Describe possible meanings from contextual evidence. Do not derive meaning solely from etymology or import every possible sense into one occurrence.
formerGuidance: The range of meanings the word carries, and what decides between them.

sections.title: Passages in context
sections.guidance: Read each significant occurrence in its sentence, paragraph, genre and historical setting. Record which sense best fits and why.
formerGuidance: The passages where the word matters most.

sections.title: Meaning and conclusion
sections.guidance: Explain what the word means in the passage under study, citing textual evidence. State uncertainties and avoid making the word carry more theology than the passage supports.
formerGuidance: What you have concluded, and what remains open.

sections.title: Application
sections.guidance: What follows for belief and life from the passage's teaching, rather than from a dictionary definition alone?

sections.title: Grammar and syntax
sections.guidance: Where helpful, examine grammatical form, syntax and discourse function. Use reputable linguistic tools; original-language expertise is optional.

sections.title: Biblical-theological connections
sections.guidance: Compare related biblical teaching while keeping each passage's own meaning distinct.
formerGuidance: What the word contributes to the Bible's teaching.
